name: CH-53E Super Stallion
summary: Three-engine heavy-lift helicopter that has carried Marine Corps vehicles, troops and cargo since the 1980s; the Navy's MH-53E Sea Dragon tows minesweeping gear.

wings: Huge seven-blade main rotor with a large dome-shaped hub fairing
No wing; stub sponsons on the lower fuselage hold the main gear
engines: Three engines: one pod on each side of the upper fuselage plus a third behind the rotor mast on the left
Intake of the third engine visible on top of the fuselage behind the rotor head
fuselage: Long fuselage with a long refueling probe extending from the right side of the nose
Sponsons on both lower sides housing retractable main gear, usually with external drop tanks hung on them
Rear loading ramp; MH-53E has even larger sponsons
Often stained with oil and grease around the rotor head and sides
tail: Tail fin canted strongly to the left
Strut-braced gull-wing (bent) horizontal stabilizer on the right side of the fin
Four-blade tail rotor at the top of the canted fin

tellTales: Seven main rotor blades and three engines on top
Fin canted sharply to one side with a bent, strut-braced gull-wing stabilizer
Drop tanks hung off the outside of the lower sponsons

confusedWith.howToTell: The E has a bent gull-wing stabilizer, a big hub fairing and drop tanks on smaller sponsons; the K has a straight stabilizer, larger clean sponsons and anhedral-tipped composite blades.
The CH-53E has a single seven-blade main rotor and a tail rotor; the Chinook has two tandem rotors and no tail rotor.
